newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold tumbles as bullion dips, yen bounces.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold tumbles as bullion dips, yen bounces.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based gold futures ended sharply lower on Thursday, depressed by continued profit taking by individual investors sparked by a drop in bullion prices and the yen's modest bounce against the dollar, traders said.
The other precious metals were dragged lower as well, with only the nearby palladium contracts closing firmer amid continued tightness in Japan's spot palladium sponge market.

TOCOM most-active December gold futures closed 15 yen lower at 1,350 yen per gram, near the bottom of the day's 1,365 to 1,349 range, after rallying on Wednesday to a 12-week high of 1,368. The remaining months were 12 to 19 yen lower.

Bullion was quoted at $350.30/60 an ounce in late Tokyo trade, extending an overnight slide in New York of nearly $2.00 to a closing quote of $351.00/50. The drop was fuelled in part by a rebound in the U.S. stock market, traders said.

Yen-based gold prices had risen sharply on Tuesday and Wednesday, reflecting a technical bounce in bullion prices from last week's three-year lows and a slump in the yen to a four-year trough against the dollar.
With sentiment toward gold bullion remaining bearish, Japanese investors with long positions have eagerly locked in profits at the higher yen-based prices, traders said.
Yen-based futures were also pressured by the yen's battle back to about 121 yen to the dollar on Thursday from a four-year low of 122.78 on Wednesday.
TOCOM December platinum ended down 16 at 1,356 yen a gram. December silver was off 2.8 yen at 190.9 yen per 10 grams.

TOCOM December palladium was off 4 yen at 469 yen per gram, although spot February was up 6 at 479 yen as the market's backwardation widened. Lengthy delays in concluding Russian supply contracts fuelled nearby tightness. New York's NYMEX palladium futures, by contrast, remained in a modest contango.
